q: Does the (F,t) → activity inversion generalize under partial-body or non-uniform internal contamination geometry (e.g. 137Cs sequestered in liver/kidney with heterogeneous dose to circulating lymphocytes)?
basis: The paper assumes whole-body, well-mixed uniform biokinetics from a single IV bolus in mice; real accidental intakes (inhalation, ingestion) will produce heterogeneous organ deposition. Turner et al. show Eq.3 whole-body retention only, and blood/spleen may see very different local dose-rates than the whole-body average. Nothing in the reproduced pipeline exercises non-uniform geometry.
next_steps: Simulate a two-compartment biokinetic model (e.g. GI + soft-tissue retention with 30/70 split, or ICRP-137 inhalation type-M) and re-run the F(A,t) inversion on synthetic bloods generated from that model. Check whether the paper's calibration curve degrades and by how much AUC drops.

q: Is protracted-dose exposure at the same integrated dose equivalent to the acute-then-decaying internal-emitter case that the paper fits?
basis: The paper's F(A,t) = b + k·A·t·exp(Q1+Q2) explicitly encodes ongoing exposure via the k·A·t term — the dose is accruing during the assay window. But external-photon biodosimetry (LNT/DDREF debate) tells us protracted dose deposits less biological damage per Gy than acute. The paper does not test whether an external chronic exposure of equal integrated dose would give the same γ-H2AX footprint at day 3.
next_steps: Run a paired external-photon protracted-exposure calibration (e.g. Cs-137 external at 0.5–5 Gy delivered over 2–14 d) in a parallel mouse cohort and compare γ-H2AX(t) curves against the internal-emitter fit. Test whether a single k parameter suffices or whether internal-vs-external requires a scaling factor.

q: What is the inter-donor coefficient-of-variation (CV) floor for γ-H2AX total fluorescence in mice, and does that CV floor set a hard LoD below which the inversion cannot resolve two nearby activities?
basis: Group SEM (n=8) is reported but individual mouse fluorescence values are NOT in the supplements — the replication cannot bound biological noise from below. Without a per-mouse variance estimate, the ROC AUC of 0.93 and the reported Pearson 0.86 may be inflated by group averaging. A real deployment sees one individual, not the mean of eight.
next_steps: Request individual-mouse fluorescence values from the authors, OR run a small in-house cohort (n≥12 per activity) at 2 activity levels close together (e.g. 6.66 vs 7.65 MBq) and directly measure CV. Recompute AUC treating each mouse as a sample (n≈160) vs group means (n=20) to quantify the ROC gap and set a real LoD.

q: How does γ-H2AX biodosimetry combine (compose vs conflict) with cytogenetic and premature-chromosome-condensation (PCC) biodosimetry in the same mouse/donor at the same time point?
basis: γ-H2AX resolves early (hours-to-days) DSB damage; dicentric-chromosome and PCC assays report at 24–48 h and out to weeks with different kinetics and different LoDs. The paper positions γ-H2AX as a standalone assay but does not test whether combining it with a PCC/dicentric readout improves the day-14 correlation (which drops to 0.34 Pearson, i.e. essentially uninformative).
next_steps: Design a paired-assay cohort: γ-H2AX + PCC on the same blood draw at days 2, 5, 14. Fit a joint (F_gH2AX, F_PCC, t) → A model and see whether the joint AUC exceeds the marginal 0.93. This directly tests whether γ-H2AX buys anything on top of the ICRU-standard cytogenetic assays for internal emitters.

q: What is the true low-dose LoD of the γ-H2AX+inversion pipeline below 0.1 Gy accrued dose, and can it discriminate against sham/control mice with a statistically defensible false-positive rate?
basis: The paper's lowest activity is 5.74 MBq (roughly 3.4 Gy accrued to day 14 per Table 1) — an order of magnitude above the operational-triage cut-off of 0.1–0.5 Gy that ICRP/WHO consider decision-relevant for population-scale radiological events. The replication reproduces the paper's regime but cannot say anything about the operationally-interesting low-dose region. The paper does not present a control-vs-lowest ROC.
next_steps: Extend the mouse cohort with 3 additional low-activity groups (e.g. 0.5, 1.0, 2.5 MBq) plus n≥12 sham controls, sampled at day 2 and day 3 (the paper's best window). Compute ROC AUC low-vs-control at each activity and report the smallest activity where AUC>0.9 with the observed CV. Publish the LoD explicitly rather than only the high-dose calibration.
